title: DVR uniqueness closes the diagonal over a Noetherian base
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and assume $S$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (its underlying space has a finite subcover for every open cover). For every discrete valuation ring $A$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, let $j:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the morphism induced by $A\hookrightarrow K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose that for any two morphisms $h_1,h_2:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$, the equalities $fh_1=fh_2$ and $h_1j=h_2j$ imply $h_1=h_2$. Then the diagonal $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_S X$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0207 (lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-separation), implication (3) to (1), finite-type Noetherian diagonal argument.

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_S X$, with projections $p_1,p_2$, and write $\Delta=\Delta_f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ is Noetherian. The projection $p_1:Y\to X$ is a base change of $f$, so is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] again to see that $Y$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-diagonal-immersion], $\Delta$ is an immersion.

source.place: Tag 0207 (lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-separation), finite-type Noetherian paragraph of the converse; Tag 0CM2 (lemma-reach-point-closure-Noetherian), restricted to points outside the image.

proof.text: The immersion $\Delta$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](2). For every affine open $V\subseteq Y$, its inverse image $\Delta^{-1}(V)$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $X$, hence is Noetherian and in particular quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Thus $\Delta$ is quasi-compact and therefore of finite type, by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0207 (lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-separation), finite-type Noetherian paragraph of the converse; Tag 0CM2 (lemma-reach-point-closure-Noetherian), restricted to points outside the image.

proof.text: If $\Delta(|X|)$ is not closed in $|Y|$, choose $y\in\overline{\Delta(|X|)}\setminus\Delta(|X|)$. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-image-boundary-dvr] to the finite-type map $\Delta:X\to Y$, with $Y$ locally Noetherian by step 1. It gives a DVR $A$, its fraction field $K$, and maps $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ and $v:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ such that $vj=\Delta u$ and $v(s_A)=y$.

source.place: Tag 0207 (lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-separation), finite-type Noetherian paragraph of the converse; Tag 0CM2 (lemma-reach-point-closure-Noetherian), restricted to points outside the image.

proof.text: Set $h_i=p_i v$. The fibre-product relation gives $fh_1=fh_2$, while $p_i\Delta=1_X$ and $vj=\Delta u$ give $h_1j=u=h_2j$. The hypothesis therefore gives $h_1=h_2$. By the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product], $v=\Delta h_1$: both maps to $Y$ have projections $h_1,h_1$. Evaluating at $s_A$ gives $y=\Delta(h_1(s_A))$, contrary to the choice of $y$. Hence $\Delta(|X|)$ is closed.

proof.text: The map $\Delta$ is an immersion by step 1 and has closed image by steps 3–4. The equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion] now makes it a closed immersion, as required.
